title: Part 3. Devakinandana Kaviraja, *Sri Vaishnavabhidhana
html:
A Sanskrit list of the names of Vaishnavas — "The Names of the Vaishnavas": a brief recapitulation of the same author's Bengali vandana (pp. 56–60 of the 1910 edition; verses 1–53)

[p. 56]

1Having first bowed to my guru Sri Purushottama,1 whose merciful glance has purified the earth — a wish-fulfilling tree that grants every desire —

2and to all the Vaishnavas — full of great power, of great fortune, great purifiers of the fallen, mahabhagavatas, forms of Vishnu —

3[I bow] then to the renowned Shachi and Jagannatha, brahmanas in form, the parents of Sri Vishvarupa and Sri Vishvambhara;

4to the blessed Vishvarupa, the great soul, bearing the name Shankararanya, in the form of the elder brother of Sri Krishna Chaitanya-chandra;

5to Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu — the Lord of Gadadhara's life, the husband of Lakshmi and Vishnupriya, prema and mercy embodied in person;

6and likewise to Padmavati and Srimat Mukunda,2 best of brahmanas — the parents, of incomparable good fortune, of Nityananda Svarupa;

7to Srimat Nityananda-chandra — the husband of Vasudha and Jahnavi, the father of Sri Virabhadra, the crusher of all the godless.

8Though I am by nature insignificant, unintelligent and a child myself, a fool in describing the endless glory of the endless Vaishnavas,

9yet from the greed of my tongue and the great agitation of my heart I make a certain remembrance — the endless names of the Vaishnavas.

10And this too I, the insignificant one, say to all: [you] in whom virtues arise, do not count against me faults against the order.

11Sri Madhava Puri,3 Srila Advaita Acharya, and likewise Achyuta, Gopinatha, Srinivasa, Govinda, Chandrashekhara,

[p. 57]

12Haridasa, Sri Murari Gupta, and likewise Narayana, Mukunda, Vasudeva, Sri Damodara Pandita,

13Pitambara, Jagannatha, Sri Narayana and Shankara, Sri Rama Pandita, and likewise Nilambara Chakravarti,

14Gangadasa, the brahmana Vishnu, Sri Sudarshana Pandita, and likewise Vidyanidhi, Buddhimanta, Srila Sadashiva,

15Shrigarbha, Shrinidhi, Shuklambara, Shridhara Pandita, Kavichandra, Ramadasa, Vanamali, Halayudha,

16Vijaya, Nandana Acharya, Ishana, Garudadhvaja, Jagadisha, Sanjaya, Shriman, and likewise Kashishvara,

17Gangadasa, Vasudeva Bhadra, Rama and Mukunda, Sri Vallabha, best of acharyas, Mishra Srila Sanatana,

18Acharya Vanamali and Kashinatha, best of brahmanas, the Puri bearing the name Ishvara, Srimat Keshava Bharati,

19the Puri named Paramananda, Damodara Svarupa,4 the Tirtha named Nrisimha, and likewise Ramachandra Puri,

20and Brahmananda Puri, Sri Satyananda Bharati, Srimat Sukhananda Puri, and likewise Sri Govinda Puri,

21the divine Garuda Avadhuta, the Puri named Raghava, Brahmananda Svarupa, the Puri Sriyuta Keshava,

22Srimat Vishnu Puri, the great soul Vishveshvarananda, the one whose name is Sri Sacchidananda, and likewise Anubhavananda,

23Srimat Krishnananda Puri, Nrisimhananda Bharati, the divine one named Kashishvara, Hanuman,5 Sri Sanatana,

[p. 58]

24Rupa, Jiva, Sri Prabodhananda, Shuddha Sarasvati, the one bearing the name Raghunatha Dasa, and likewise Gopala Bhatta,

25Raghunatha, Lokanatha, Srimat the one named Bhugarbha, Raghava, Jagadananda Pandita, Sri Purandara,

26Kashi Mishra, Raya Ramananda, the brahmana Vakreshvara, Vaninatha Pattanayaka, and likewise Govindananda,

27Sadashiva Kaviraja, Gadadhara of the Dasa family, Sri Shivananda Sena and Sri Mukunda, best of physicians,

28Srimat Narahari, and likewise Srila Raghunandana, Raghunatha Dasa the vaidya, Upadhyaya Madhusudana,

29Devananda, best of brahmanas, Srila Acharya Purandara, Sriyuta Acharyachandra, Sri Krishnadasa Pandita,

30the [Lord's] fellow student Paramananda, and likewise Srimat Srishtidhara,6 Govinda, Madhava and Vasudeva, bearing the name Ghosha,

31Srila Sri Ramadasa and Sri Sundarananda, Sri Parameshvara and my supreme one — Srila Sri Purushottama,7

32Sri Krishnadasa, Sri Gauridasa, Sri Kamalakara, Sri Vamshivadana Dasa, who revealed the song of the flute,

33Srimat Uddharana and Srila the brahmana Sri Purushottama, Kaviraja Mishra, the best [of all], Madhusudana Pandita,

34Srimat Bhagavatacharya, and likewise Govinda Acharya, Sri Sarvabhauma, and likewise Sriyuta Nandana Acharya,

35Srimat Prataparudra, Yadunatha […],8 the brahmana Haridasa, Srila Saranga, Makaradhvaja,

[p. 59]

36Sri Vrindavana Dasa, the Pandita named Jagadisha, Pradyumna Mishra, Tapana Acharya, and likewise Sri Bhagavan,9

37Sri Vipradasa the Oriya, the vaidya Sri Vishnudasa, the vaidya Vanamali Dasa, Haridasa, Gadadhara,

38Sri Krishnadasa the Oriya, Sri Kashishvara Pandita, Balarama Dasa and Jagannatha Dasa, Sri Chandaneshvara,

39Simheshvara, Shivananda, Balarama Mahiti,10 Subuddhi Mishra, Tulasi Mishra, the one called Shrinatha,

40Kashinatha, Hari Bhatta, Madhava Pattanayaka, Ramananda Vasu, the brahmachari Sri Purushottama,

41the brahmana Sri Ramachandra, Srimat Shrikara Pandita, Yadunatha Kavichandra, Pandita Sri Dhananjaya,

42Acharya Sri Jagannatha, Sri Suryadasa Pandita, Srila Sri Lakshmana Acharya, and likewise Sri Krishna Acharya,

43Chaitanya Dasa, the physician Paramananda Gupta, Sri Jagannatha and Kamsari — the Senas, Sriyuta Bhaskara,

44Kavichandra, Sri Mukunda, Sri Rama, Vallabha Sena, Sriyuta the one named Balarama Dasa, Mahesha Pandita,

45Paramananda Avadhuta, Sri Gangadasa Pandita, Kaviraja Sri Mukunda,11 Sri Jiva Pandita,

46Chiranjiva, Krishnadasa, the boy named Krishnadasa, the excellent Yadunatha Dasa, Sri Krishnadasa Pandita,

47Rama Tirtha, Krishna Tirtha, the Puri Sri Purushottama, Srimat Jagannatha Tirtha, and likewise Raghunatha Puri,

[p. 60]

48Sri Vasudeva Tirtha and Srila the one named Upendra Ashrama, the Puri named Ananta, Hariharananda Bharati,

49Srimat Nrisimha Chaitanya, Srimat Acharya Madhava, Shankara, Madhavananda Acharya, Dasa Sanatana, Shivananda Chakravarti, the brahmana Narayana and others.

50Whoever remembers them at dawn or hears [their names] with devotion will at no time come to torment — this is certain.

51The person who, remembering them again and again, bows down will never commit an offence at the feet of the Vaishnavas.

52By merely remembering them he attains the position of a Vaishnava and bhakti, sweet with the nectar of prema, hard to attain even for the gods.

53The Vaishnava is above all; he surpasses all the Vedas; and he is far beyond hearing, sight and mind.

Thus ends the Vaishnavabhidhana composed by Sri Devakinandana Kaviraja.

Obeisance to the Vaishnavas — wish-fulfilling trees, oceans of mercy, purifiers of the fallen — obeisance, obeisance!

To those devoted to the name of Hari and wholly given to devotion to Hari — whether their conduct be bad or good — to them obeisance, obeisance for ever!12

Offered to Sri Krishna.

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. Purushottama Dasa, the author's guru (Part 2, v. 87). According to Majumdar this is merely a list of names: apart from Nityananda and Virabhadra no one in it is described, not even the author's guru; Majumdar therefore thinks it unlikely that Jiva's vandana was composed on its basis. The order of names almost coincides with Devakinandana's Bengali vandana (Part 2).
  2. Nityananda's father (in the Bengali vandana — Hadai Pandita, Part 2, v. 10); GGD 40.
  3. Madhavendra Puri.
  4. Here, in the place of "Damodara Puri" of the Bengali vandana (Part 2, v. 46), we have "Damodara Svarupa": perhaps Svarupa Damodara.
  5. The reading is unclear (hanupāmaḥ); possibly a corruption. In Part 2 at this place there are Rupa and Sanatana (v. 53).
  6. Srishtidhara is unknown from other sources; there is no counterpart at this place in the Bengali vandana.
  7. "My supreme one" — the author's guru (cf. v. 1 and Part 2, v. 87).
  8. The reading is unclear (yadunāthadhavāmaraḥ); in Part 2, v. 106 — the brahmana Yadunatha.
  9. Tapana Acharya (Tapana Mishra?) and Bhagavan (Acharya) are not in the Bengali vandana; Tapana Mishra — CC Adi 16 and Madhya 17 (Kashi); Bhagavan Acharya — CC Antya 2.
  10. "Balarama Mahattama" — apparently "Mahiti" (Part 2, v. 114).
  11. The edition has "Kaviraja Sri Mukunda-ananda": possibly "Mukunda" merged with a neighbouring word.
  12. These two verses after the colophon are a well-known prayer of obeisance to the Vaishnavas (the first is the traditional pranama-mantra), apparently added by a copyist or the editor.
